dram_configuration.drain_contract: The external runner attempts at most one request per memory tick and continues ticking until all callbacks complete.
dram_configuration.scope_boundary: This is a single-channel DRAM-controller sensitivity probe, not a complete HBM stack, accelerator, or serving system.

hypothesis_source_context.observed_boundary: The pinned sparse top-k output is score-descending rather than address-sorted. Address sorting is a kernel/hardware hypothesis, and page clustering is a model/indexer architecture-change hypothesis.

metadata.oracle_scope: patched Ramulator2 HBM3 synthetic address-order and page-locality sensitivity with complete callback drain

bf16_mla_record_1152b.scope: 36 contiguous HBM transactions per selected token matching one synthetic one-layer 1,152-byte BF16 MLA record

representative_hbm_transaction_32b.scope: one representative HBM transaction per selected token

workload.logical_address_sort_boundary: The address-sorted case orders ascending logical token positions. It does not sort the mapped HBM address-vector tuple.
workload.mapping: Each 64-token synthetic page maps across 64 HBM bank domains before advancing row. The representative geometry maps one token to one 32-byte column transaction. The BF16 geometry maps each token to 36 contiguous 32-byte transactions and each page to nine rows in the same bank domain.
workload.trace_fidelity: synthetic probes only; the BF16 geometry represents one synthetic one-layer record and neither geometry reproduces full multi-layer GLM DSA, MLA, indexer, cache, scale, GPU traffic, overlap, or execution

compatibility_patch.reason: AppleClang 16 rejects the pinned source without the standard dependent-template disambiguator.

source_identity.selection_reason: The official v2.1.0 stable tag supports HBM3/HBM4 pseudochannels, exposes Python-native structured controller statistics, and includes the newer validation workflows and aggregated fixes. It supersedes the v2.0a baseline without using an unreleased branch.
